transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-12
Time: 14:00 ET
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Mark Reynolds (CTO, Acadia), Sofia Lang (Head of Compliance), Evan Ortiz (Infra Manager), Lena Park (Legal)

Auto-generated summary: initial compliance/discovery - medium transcription quality

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood Inference. maybe quick intros?
[00:12] Mark Reynolds: Mark, CTO at Acadia Regional Bank, we've got Sofia on compliance, Evan infra, Lena legal. thanks.
[00:20] Sofia Lang: hi.
[00:22] Evan Ortiz: hey all.
[00:28] Jordan Lee: cool. today's agenda — understand your residency and logging requirements, whether hosted is an option, or if Dedicated/Private required, and next steps for a pilot.
[00:45] Priya Patel: hi i'm Priya, SE. i'll jump into some technical Qs after we hear requirements.
[00:52] Mark Reynolds: high level — we want an LLM feature for internal summaries and customer support triage. main blockers: data cannot leave US for some flows, PII masking required, and audit logs have to be controlled.
[01:10] Sofia Lang: to add — for certain products we fall under GLBA and some customer data could be HIPAA adjacent. We need to understand how logs are stored and who has access, and retention windows.
[01:30] Jordan Lee: totally. quick clarifying Q: when you say "cannot leave US" is that account-level only, or certain datasets?
[01:40] Mark Reynolds: mostly account-level, but also some product lines need EU residency for EU customers. so we need both region isolation and per-tenant routing ideally.
[01:55] Priya Patel: that's doable. Redwood supports regional routing and you can pin models to region-specific hosts. for Hosted API we have region selector for some models, but there are limitations on guaranteed isolation unless you use Dedicated or Private.
[02:15] Evan Ortiz: can you clarify limitations? what data still touches any Redwood control plane?
[02:22] Priya Patel: good q. hosted calls go through Redwood control plane in our hosted region; metadata/metrics may be aggregated unless you opt-in for minimal logging. for strict isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private — Dedicated gives reserved gpu pools and network isolation, but control plane still in Redwood's managed environment; Private is our VPC/on-prem option where control plane can be customer-managed.
[02:55] Sofia Lang: and encryption? kms? we must use our own KMS for keys at rest.
[03:04] Jordan Lee: we integrate with customer KMS (KMS/HSM) for Private and for Dedicated we offer KMS integrations, but Hosted uses Redwood-managed keys by default — we can discuss Bring Your Own Key for Dedicated in contract.
[03:20] Lena Park: any SOC/ISO reports you can share? we need SOC2, ISO27001 and HIPAA BAAs if applicable.
[03:30] Jordan Lee: yes i'll share SOC2 and our security whitepaper after the call. we can support HIPAA under a BAA for Dedicated/Private customers.
[03:41] Mark Reynolds: ok good. what's your typical retention for logs on hosted?
[03:47] Priya Patel: default hosted retention is 90 days for request logs; you can configure shorter, and for PII we offer redaction options and disable request logs entirely for sensitive routes. but compliance teams often want audit logs separate — for Dedicated/Private we can stream logs to customer S3 or SIEM.
[04:10] Evan Ortiz: streaming logs — is that push or pull? and can we point to our existing SIEM behind firewall?
[04:18] Priya Patel: we can push via secure connection (TLS) to your S3 in a VPC endpoint, or integrate with common SIEMs. for Private deployments it's all internal to your VPC so it's straightforward.
[04:35] Mark Reynolds: what's the delta in latency/cost between Hosted and Dedicated? we care about per-token cost for at-scale.
[04:45] Jordan Lee: generally Hosted is lower ops overhead and can be cost-effective at low volume. Dedicated reduces per-token costs by predictable batching and reserved capacity, Dedicated can be 20-40% cheaper depending on workload. Private has additional ops overhead and hardware costs to you. these are rough numbers; Priya can run model-specific bench.
[05:05] Priya Patel: yes, i'll need a few sample prompts and throughput targets to estimate. also quantization/profile choices affect CPU/GPU usage.
[05:18] Sofia Lang: important — we cannot allow raw customer PII into third-party logs. can Redwood support on-the-fly token redaction before logs persist?
[05:28] Priya Patel: we have prefix/PII masking options and token-level redaction in the request pipeline, though sometimes transcriptions mislabel tokens. we'll document typical coverage. for absolute certainty, Private gives you full control — logs never leave your network.
[05:46] Mark Reynolds: what about GDPR subject-access requests? If EU customer requests deletion, can we delete associated vectors/embeddings and logs?
[05:55] Jordan Lee: yes — we support data deletion APIs. for Hosted we delete per our retention policy and can accelerate deletions on request, but you should treat Hosted less as absolute deletion guarantees compared to Private where you control storage.
[06:10] Evan Ortiz: are embeddings stored by default? we plan to use embeddings for search.
[06:16] Priya Patel: embeddings can be cached; by default Hosted caches to improve perf. we can disable caching or ensure it's stored in your region. Dedicated/Private gives full control over cache storage.
[06:33] Lena Park: legal Q — if we bring Redwood into a pilot, what indemnities or liabilities exist around data leakage?
[06:42] Jordan Lee: standard contracts have liability caps; for enterprise deals we negotiate tailored terms. i'll loop in legal after you share your procurement requirements.
[06:55] Sofia Lang: do you support HIPAA de-id processes or are we expected to handle that pre-ingest?
[07:02] Priya Patel: we recommend pre-ingest de-identification for highly sensitive data. we can also run redaction routines on ingestion and flag risky tokens, but it's safer to do pre-ingest pipeline in your infra.
[07:18] Mark Reynolds: do you have customers in banking who run Private? any references?
[07:24] Jordan Lee: yes — a few regional banks use our Dedicated/Private offerings; i'll get permission to share anonymized references.
[07:32] Priya Patel: technical note — for Private we support both VPC-hosted control planes and fully on-prem options; for on-prem there is a larger deployment window (4-8 weeks typically).
[07:50] Evan Ortiz: what are required network changes for Private? firewall rules, NAT, etc?
[07:58] Priya Patel: we provide a network runbook. typical changes: VPC peering or private link, cert-based auth, and opening outbound TLS to certain Redwood registries if you're using our images; but fully air-gapped on-prem is possible with extra steps.
[08:18] Mark Reynolds: timeline — we're aiming to pilot in prod-adjacent env by July. is that realistic?
[08:25] Jordan Lee: yes, on a Dedicated pilot definitely; Private might be tight but possible if procurement is fast.
[08:33] Sofia Lang: procurement note — we need a BAA and a data processing addendum before pilot.
[08:40] Jordan Lee: got it. i'll include DPA/BAA templates.
[08:44] Lena Park: any special logging restrictions for EU data? we want logs for investigation but cannot store raw PII.
[08:53] Priya Patel: we can pseudonymize and hash identifiers before log storage, and provide policy for masking; archiving can be done to customer-controlled storage in EU region.
[09:08] Mark Reynolds: on the technical deep-dive, i'd like to validate KV cache behavior — does it persist across model versions and how does eviction work?
[09:18] Priya Patel: KV cache is managed per instance; with Dedicated you get control over cache policies and can snapshot or flush on rollout; Hosted has ephemeral caches and automatic eviction policies. sometimes docs say KV "cash" in transcripts — apologies for that.
[09:35] Jordan Lee: ha, yes transcription error.
[09:38] Evan Ortiz: also interested in telemetry — can we disable token-level telemetry?
[09:44] Priya Patel: yes, we can disable token-level telemetry for specific routes. aggregate metrics still available for billing unless you opt for custom billing integrations in Dedicated.
[10:00] Mark Reynolds: let's talk about pilot scope — we want to run summarization on internal tickets and external customer emails. SLA wise we expect 200ms p50 for short prompts and < 1s p95. can your infra meet that?
[10:15] Priya Patel: depends on model and route; with Dedicated and optimized model selection we can meet sub-second p95 for many models. we'll propose test vectors.
[10:28] Jordan Lee: next — pricing sensitivity: what's your budget?
[10:33] Mark Reynolds: looking to validate value; budgets TBD but we need to understand unit economics to forecast.
[10:40] Priya Patel: i'll include a cost model for hosted vs dedicated vs private based on throughput.
[10:46] Sofia Lang: any certification for record-keeping? we need immutable audit trails for certain investigations.
[10:54] Priya Patel: for Dedicated/Private we can stream append-only audit logs to your S3 with object locking, or to your SIEM, to maintain immutability.
[11:06] Lena Park: legal — can logs be segmented per product line? we have cross-product teams.
[11:13] Jordan Lee: yes, routing policies and per-route logs let you separate flows.
[11:20] Mark Reynolds: curious if Redwood supports data residency routing by tenancy.
[11:25] Priya Patel: yes — routing policies can send traffic to different regions or model variants based on tenant ID. for Hosted there are some constraints on strict guarantees. Dedicated/Private recommended for per-tenant isolation.
[11:40] Evan Ortiz: operational runbook — who handles patching for Dedicated?
[11:45] Priya Patel: Redwood manages the serving runtime and autoscaling for Dedicated, but you control deployment config; for Private on-prem you manage patching unless you subscribe to a managed service.
[11:58] Jordan Lee: quick demo offer — we can set up a 60-min technical demo of a Dedicated node with sample traffic if helpful.
[12:05] Mark Reynolds: yes please, include latency/cost spreadsheet.
[12:10] Priya Patel: noted. i'll propose dates in the follow-up.
[12:15] Sofia Lang: compliance question — are you able to redact sensitive fields in model outputs as well (PII in completion)?
[12:24] Priya Patel: we have output filters and can run deterministic scrubbers pre- or post-inference. for high-sensitivity flows we recommend post-processing in your infra.
[12:36] Mark Reynolds: any data residency certifications for EU data centers?
[12:41] Jordan Lee: we host in multiple cloud regions and can provision EU-hosted Dedicated capacity; for Private you can run entirely in your EU region. i'll share region list.
[12:52] Evan Ortiz: network egress — will traffic to hosted endpoints egress through a particular region or is it tied to model host?
[12:59] Priya Patel: egress is tied to the model host's region. we'll document endpoints per region.
[13:10] Mark Reynolds: we need a clear list of what metadata Redwood captures by default.
[13:15] Jordan Lee: we'll produce a metadata collection table (default fields, retention). action item for us to share that.
[13:24] Sofia Lang: also provide DPA specifics around subprocessors.
[13:29] Jordan Lee: will include subprocessors list.
[13:34] Evan Ortiz: operational costs for Private — any rough hardware profiles?
[13:39] Priya Patel: yes typical configs and GPU types; i'll include in pilot docs.
[13:44] Mark Reynolds: ok next steps recap?
[13:47] Jordan Lee: summary — we'll send SOC2 + security whitepaper, DPA/BAA template, region list, metadata table, and Priya will send pilot plan + cost estimate. you (Mark) will share data classification and retention policy. we'll schedule a Dedicated demo/benchmark next week.
[14:10] Lena Park: timeline for documents?
[14:12] Jordan Lee: SOC2/whitepaper and DPA by 5/14; pilot plan by 5/19; schedule demo 5/18-5/22.
[14:20] Mark Reynolds: sounds good.
[14:22] Sofia Lang: thanks everyone.
[14:25] Jordan Lee: thanks, we'll follow up via email with links.
[14:30] Priya Patel: thanks all.
[14:32] End of transcript
